questions.q: What does a Glue job bookmark track for an S3 source?
options: The set of files (and their timestamps) already processed by that job
The IAM role used to run the job
The total dollar cost of all previous job runs
The Data Catalog database name only
questions.explain: For S3 sources, bookmark state is typically tracked as the files (and timestamps) already read by that job.

questions.q: When does a job's bookmark state actually advance?
options: Only when the job calls job.commit() at the end of a successful run
Continuously, every second the job is running
As soon as the job starts, regardless of outcome
Only when a crawler runs afterward
questions.explain: Bookmark state updates on job.commit() after a successful run — a failed run never advances it.

questions.q: What happens if a bookmarked job fails partway through and is retried?
options: It does not skip the data it was working on, since the bookmark never advanced on the failed run
It permanently loses track of all previously bookmarked data
It automatically skips the first half of the source data
The retry is blocked entirely until the bookmark is manually reset
questions.explain: Since a failed run never advances the bookmark, a retry safely reprocesses the same data rather than skipping it.

questions.q: Why would a data engineer deliberately turn bookmarks off for a job?
options: For a small reference/dimension table meant to be fully replaced on every run
Because bookmarks are required for every Glue job to function at all
Because bookmarks always cause incorrect output
Because bookmarks only work with Scala Spark, not PySpark
questions.explain: For jobs meant to fully reprocess a small dataset every time, leaving bookmarks off is simpler than managing incremental state.

questions.q: What is a 'bookmark reset' used for?
options: Explicitly forcing the next run to reprocess everything, e.g. after fixing a bug in transform logic
Automatically running every night at midnight
Deleting the job's Data Catalog table
Switching a job from PySpark to Scala Spark
questions.explain: A bookmark reset is an explicit action that clears tracked state, forcing a full reprocess on the next run.
